correctness.rationale: The triangular blocks are individually entire semigroups. For |arg z|≤θ<π/2 the off-diagonal is bounded by n^γ/(e n! cos θ), while both diagonals are at most one in modulus. This gives strong continuity by density at zero; truncations converge in norm locally on the open right half-plane and at every positive real time, proving holomorphy and immediate compactness. The generator is the diagonal block operator on its maximal graph domain, with finite supports a core by truncation. Away from its listed eigenvalues its block inverses have diagonal entries O(1/(n!)²) and upper-right entries O(n^γ/(n!)³), excluding additional spectrum. For Re z<0 the first diagonal diverges; on the imaginary axis the supremum of the off-diagonal moduli is finite exactly under the factorial-distance criterion, by the two-sided sine bound. The right half-plane is the interior of the boundedness set and no extension through an axis point can agree with the blocks on an open neighborhood. For γ>1 the integer error in the nearest-integer recurrence eventually vanishes; the remaining signed error must vanish since it would otherwise grow by factorial factors. For γ≤1 use the canonical factorial expansion with a tail strictly less than the maximal tail (take terminating digits at ambiguous endpoints). In a fixed bound class, digit counts are O_C(1+n^(1−γ)); covers at size 1/N! give the stated upper bounds. For γ<1, restricting digits to 0 through floor(j^(1−γ)/4) keeps the points in the group; equal-weight cylinder mass is exp(−(1−γ)N log N+O(N)). An interval between the two successive factorial scales has positive-mass intersection with at most two level-N cylinders, giving a Frostman bound for each s<1−γ. Binary factorial digits give uncountably many points at γ=1. Multiplication by n! modulo 1 preserves Lebesgue measure, so the fixed bound classes are null; the subgroup property, rational density and exact group of translations follow directly. Bounded analyticity is sectorial (proper subsectors), not a uniform bound on the full half-plane. Finite diagnostics were inspected but not run; the proof, not those diagnostics, establishes the infinite statements.
